Got it. You want this to feel like a **peer-to-peer ask**, not a pitch, so it flies under the radar and actually gets engagement.

Here’s a version that’s safe, natural, and non-solicit-y:

---

Hey everyone 🤍

We recently went through a full rebrand on our med spa growth company and are about ~60 days into working with a new social media team.

I’d love some *honest feedback* from other owners who are in the trenches day-to-day on what you look for when evaluating social performance early on.

Things like:
• What metrics actually matter to you in the first 60–90 days?  
• What would you consider “good” growth vs. concerning?  
• At what point do you usually decide to pivot teams or strategy?

I’m less concerned with vanity metrics and more focused on whether what we’re seeing is *actually translating into brand authority and future pipeline*.

If anyone is open to taking a quick look and sharing their perspective, I’m happy to DM our IG so it stays within group rules.

Appreciate this group always, you all keep it real 🙌

---

### Why this works (so you don’t get flagged):
- No direct link in the post  
- You invite DMs instead (huge difference for moderators)  
- You ask for **advice**, not clients  
- You position yourself as a peer, not a vendor  
- You make it about *learning*, not promotion  

---

If you want a slightly bolder version that still stays safe but increases DMs, I can tweak it to subtly make people *want* to see your page.

You want this to feel like **insight + transparency**, not “go follow us.”

The move on entity["mobile_app","LinkedIn","professional networking app"] is to frame it as a **case study / build-in-public moment** and let curiosity pull people to your entity["mobile_app","Instagram","social media platform"].

Here are a few clean options you can post:

---

### Option 1: “Build in Public” (best performing style)

We just completed a full rebrand at Luxora and are ~60 days into rebuilding our social presence from scratch.

A few early observations:

• Content that educates > content that impresses  
• Founder-led perspective is outperforming polished brand posts  
• Consistency is beating creativity (for now)

Still early, but it’s been interesting to watch what actually moves vs. what we *thought* would.

Documenting the process as we go. Curious to see where this lands by day 90.

---

### Option 2: “Contrarian Insight”

Hot take after 60 days of rebuilding our social post-rebrand:

Most med spa brands don’t have a content problem. They have a positioning problem.

You can post daily, have great visuals, even decent engagement…  
and still not generate real pipeline.

We’re reworking everything around authority > aesthetics this time.

Early signals are already telling us more than the last year did.

---

### Option 3: “Soft Curiosity Hook”

We’re about 60 days into a full social reset after our rebrand.

Not optimizing for followers.  
Not optimizing for likes.

Only looking at one thing:  
Does this content make the *right* people lean in?

Some interesting patterns already emerging.

---

### Why these work:
- No “follow us” ask  
- No link dumping  
- Feels like operator insight, not marketing  
- Creates curiosity so people *choose* to click your profile → IG  

---

### If you want a subtle boost (without being obvious):
Comment on your own post after 10–15 mins:

> Had a few people ask where we’re documenting this, it’s all on IG for now.

That’s the quiet conversion play without looking thirsty.
